messages.content: What kind of fertilizer is best for growing tomatoes?

function.name: soil_analysis_analyze_soil_type
function.description: Analyze a type of soil and provides characteristics about it. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

soil_type.description: The type of the soil. For example, loam, sandy, etc.

parameters_needed.description: Optional specific characteristics of the soil to analyze.

message.content: The best fertilizer for tomatoes depends on your soil’s current nutrient levels and pH. Generally, tomatoes thrive on a balanced NPK mix with a slightly higher phosphorus (P) and potassium (K) ratio to promote root development and fruit set. A common recommendation is a 5-10-10 or 4-8-8 blend. If your soil test shows low nitrogen, you might add a separate nitrogen source like urea or fish emulsion. Organic options such as compost, well‑aged manure, bone meal, or kelp meal also work well, especially if you prefer a more natural approach. Always follow the label instructions and consider doing a soil test first to tailor the fertilizer precisely to your garden’s needs.
